minutes.headline: Board ended the old primary school senior housing deal and sent the building to the reuse committee.
minutes.summary: The Select Board honored a departing member, then approved a community bonfire, three one-day liquor licenses, five Fitchburg Gas and Electric poles on Chase Road, and a liquor license transfer for Hadwin Park Market. It declared the old primary school no longer committed to the senior housing project and added it to the building reuse committee's list. In committee reports, a member described special education funding gaps and the school committee's budget shortfall.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to release the old primary school from the Eagle Heights senior housing project and asked the building reuse committee to add it to its list.
The board approved five new Fitchburg Gas and Electric poles on Chase Road, subject to an as-built plan.
The board approved a community bonfire for June 21, two one-day liquor licenses, and a liquor license transfer for Hadwin Park Market.
In committee reports, a member said out-of-district special education costs are rising while state circuit breaker reimbursement is nearly flat.
The board set its next meeting for May 20 and said it will consider a joint workshop with the planning board.

why_it_matters: The old primary school is no longer tied to senior housing, so its future use now goes through the building reuse committee, which affects what happens to a town-owned building and its upkeep costs.
Mandated special education and English learner costs are rising faster than state reimbursement, which adds pressure on the school budget and on the town budget, mostly taxes.
